- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope after peak.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.6) and price is trending up, model often overestimates momentum; cap forecast growth at 3–5% above recent 7-day moving average.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings >0.3 in 3-day window), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and smooth transitions to avoid abrupt reversals.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >15% above recent 30-day average, reduce by 2–4% per day until convergence; if below, add 1–3% per day to avoid underestimating recovery.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates downward pressure in low-sentiment periods; add 1–3% buffer below forecast if sentiment <0.3 for 5+ consecutive days.
